summary: This is a instruction document for creating new task entries in a backlog system. It describes a six-step process: get a task description from the user, check the `.todos/` directory exists, scan existing tasks to avoid duplicates, generate the next sequential ID number, write a standardized markdown file with that ID and task details, then report back to the user.

explanations.4: This line lists which tools the AI is allowed to use when following these instructions — basic bash commands for listing and finding files, a custom script to get the next ID number, and the ability to read and write files.
explanations.19: The slug is a short, URL-friendly version of the task name using only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens (like 'add-user-login' instead of 'Add User Login').
explanations.31: Rather than manually figuring out what number to use, always run this script which looks at all existing task files and returns the next available number, ensuring no conflicts.
explanations.33: NNNN means a 4-digit number with leading zeros (like 0042), and the script pads shorter numbers with zeros automatically.
explanations.37: The filename itself never changes — it's the permanent identity of the task. Information like priority or status goes inside the file as metadata, not in the filename.
explanations.43: These bullet points are metadata fields that other tools parse; they're set to safe defaults here and the user can edit them later as the task evolves.
